speaker: EN_A
text: Welcome to KC Desk Notes. Today we are unpacking one fresh research report and the question it raises.

speaker: EN_A
text: Workday just reported its fiscal first-quarter results, and the stock popped 11 percent after hours.

speaker: EN_B
text: That’s right. It was a beat on sUBScription revenue, margins, and EPS, and it came after a tough fourth quarter and fairly bearish expectations.

speaker: EN_A
text: So what was the main surprise that changed the narrative?

speaker: EN_B
text: The headline is that Workday delivered its best first quarter for new net annual contract value in five years.

speaker: EN_B
text: And they gave more concrete details on how AI can drive revenue.

speaker: EN_A
text: Concrete details—that’s what investors have been waiting for. What did they actually lay out?

speaker: EN_B
text: They outlined three clear monetization paths for AI. First, selling their own AI agents and taking full responsibility for total cost of ownership. Second,

speaker: EN_B
text: growing their Extend Pro platform so customers can build their own AI applications on top of Workday.

speaker: EN_A
text: And the third path?

speaker: EN_B
text: Providing the APIs and infrastructure for an ecosystem of third-party developers. So it’s not just one AI product—it’s a whole platform strategy.

speaker: EN_A
text: That sounds ambitious. But does the core business still have momentum?

speaker: EN_B
text: Yes, but it’s stable rather than accelerating. If you strip out AI-related revenue,

speaker: EN_B
text: core sUBScription growth has been around 12 percent for five straight quarters. The AI layer is what could reaccelerate growth.

speaker: EN_A
text: And they also announced entry into IT service management. Why does that matter?

speaker: EN_B
text: It expands their total addressable market beyond HR and finance into the employee lifecycle more broadly. It’s a logical extension of their domain expertise.

speaker: EN_A
text: So the beat was solid, and the AI narrative is getting more tangible. But the report still keeps a Neutral rating. Why?

speaker: EN_B
text: Because a sustained re-rating depends on successful rollout of organically built AI agents and product-market fit for these newer offerings.

speaker: EN_B
text: The next twelve months are really a transition year.

speaker: EN_A
text: So what’s the one thing the report doesn’t fully settle?

speaker: EN_B
text: Whether the “headless” enterprise software vision actually drives material revenue growth, or if it’s still an experiment.

speaker: EN_B
text: The full report goes deeper into that risk and the valuation framework.

speaker: EN_A
text: Good point. We’ll leave that for the community discussion.

speaker: EN_B
text: Exactly. There’s a lot more in the full note on the GAAP-based valuation change and the margin trajectory. Worth a read if you’re following the software space.
